purpose: Fill DISTRIBUTED-DB-SCORING.md §2.1 #6 (chaos/failover) and §3.3.1, comparing against TiDB/CockroachDB/YugabyteDB on the same vm-6node crossregion topology (3 IDC + 3 GCP), per Stage 5 of phase-crossregion/GALERA-EXECUTION-PLAN.md.
design_note: Galera has no leader/follower concept, so the existing F1/C4/F2/C1/C7 framework was not reused as-is: F1/C4 were replaced by a new scenario (G1, single-node kill with an IDC/GCP region axis instead of leader/follower), F2's mechanism was reused but reinterpreted (G2, quorum-loss rather than regional-failover-survival, since 3/6 nodes is below Galera's 6-node majority of 4), C1 and C7 were reused nearly as-is with a galera branch added (G4, G5), and G3 (dual-write conflict storm) is genuinely new with no equivalent in the other three DBs' framework.

prepare.note: W=128 TPC-C schema/data load shared by all 5 G-scenarios below; no timed workload run, prepare phase only.

G1_node_kill.result_summary: rto_sec=null (outage_observed=false, 432/432 probes ok), rpo_lost_tx_count=0 — killing 1/6 nodes had zero observable write impact (5/6 still ≥ majority=4).
G1_node_kill.note: An earlier attempt at this same scenario failed due to a probe-rto-driver.sh auth bug (password never passed) and was discarded before being fetched — not preserved locally, superseded by this clean rerun.

G2_quorum_loss.params: idc_hosts=172.24.40.32,.33,.34 (all 3 killed simultaneously via systemctl stop mysql) gcp_host=10.160.152.11
G2_quorum_loss.result_summary: cluster_rebuild_sec=22.169, write_recovery_sec=22.169 (quorum reform and first successful write coincided). write-reject-validation.txt verdict=UNEXPECTED_WRITE_SUCCEEDED_review_manually — an INSERT/DELETE probe ~14s post-kill actually succeeded (empty/silent mysql output, not an error), most likely because the surviving 3-node GCP minority had not yet detected the peer loss (Galera evs.suspect_timeout/evs.inactive_timeout not yet elapsed) and briefly kept accepting writes before self-demoting to non-Primary. This is a genuine finding about write-reject detection latency, not a script bug — see DISTRIBUTED-DB-SCORING.md for full fact/inference framing.
G2_quorum_loss.destructive_note: Most destructive scenario — run last per script's own header guidance. Cluster confirmed fully healed (6/6 Primary/Synced) afterward before proceeding to fetch/teardown.

G3_dualwrite_conflict.result_summary: idc_injector: ok=1048 err=0; gcp_injector: ok=801 err=0. But wsrep counter DELTA (before/after this specific 30s window, first time captured this way rather than a post-run single-point snapshot) shows real conflict: cluster_total_delta wsrep_local_cert_failures=474, wsrep_local_bf_aborts=313 across wsrep_local_commits delta=1849 (~25.6%/~16.9%). Client-visible err=0 despite this is explained by wsrep_retry_autocommit=1 (confirmed via SHOW VARIABLES) transparently retrying single-statement autocommit UPDATEs — go-tpc's multi-statement PAYMENT transactions are not eligible for this auto-retry, which is the most likely explanation for why §3.6.2's real TPC-C run showed much higher client-visible error rates than this synthetic single-statement hammer.

G4_partition.params: duration=30s, bidirectional iptables DROP between all 3 IDC and all 3 GCP hosts
G4_partition.result_summary: error-rate-by-sec.txt (coarse SELECT-1 probe) shows 100% ok throughout — but SELECT 1 never touches InnoDB/wsrep, so this only proves mysqld stayed responsive, not that writes succeeded. A short supplementary manual re-partition (not part of the main C1/G4 script, artifacts in the '-write-probe' dir) directly tested writes: IDC side got 'Error 1213 Deadlock', GCP side got 'Error 1047 WSREP has not yet prepared node for application use' — confirming both 3-node halves correctly refused writes (both below majority=4). Cluster auto-healed back to 6/6 Primary within ~20-30s of restore, no manual intervention needed.
G4_partition.known_limitation: This supplementary write-probe used a separate, shorter (~20s) ad-hoc partition rather than reusing the main script's --duration 30 run, since the main run's own probe design (SELECT 1) turned out to be uninformative for write-availability. Both partitions used the same mechanism (iptables DROP, same CIDRs).

G5_disk_slow.result_summary: fio contention launched successfully (fio_launch_ok=true after installing fio, which was missing on this freshly-built VM); induced latency delta must be read from io-latency-p99.txt/fio-summary.txt directly, no pass/fail verdict computed by this script by design (matches TiDB/CRDB/YBDB's C7 methodology).

environment.deployed_via: make phase1 && make phase2 && make phase-galera-deploy (fresh rebuild, 2026-08-13)
environment.teardown: terraform destroy on both iac-idc and iac-gcp after this fetch, per established practice.
